title: Rabbi David Tawil: Life Lessons From Pirke Abot- "Hillel - Accountability"

chapters.title: Introduction and Personal Accountability
chapters.about: Class announcements and a story about taking responsibility.

chapters.title: Hillel's First Statement on Self and Others
chapters.about: Analyzing Hillel's teaching on self-care, ownership, and balancing needs.

chapters.title: Faith in Hashem and Personal Responsibility
chapters.about: How faith should not be used to avoid accountability for poor decisions.

chapters.title: Being a Leader in a Place Without Men
chapters.about: Hillel's teaching on leadership, taking charge, and the challenges of leadership.

chapters.title: The Bystander Effect and Neutrality
chapters.about: Psychology experiments, human nature, and the danger of staying silent.

chapters.title: Pharaoh's Advisors: Bilam, Yov, and Yitro
chapters.about: Midrash about Pharaoh's advisors and why keeping quiet is considered an action.

summary: Rabbi Tawil discusses accountability and taking personal responsibility based on statements from Pirke Abot. He explores Hillel's teachings regarding self-reliance versus responsibility to others, and examines the lessons of leadership and bystander behavior through a Midrash about Pharaoh's advisors.
questions: What does Hillel's statement 'If I am not for myself, who will be for me?' mean in daily life?
How can having faith in Hashem sometimes interfere with personal accountability?
Why does staying neutral when witnessing wrongdoing count as doing something negative?
What do the rabbinical sources say about Pharaoh's three advisors?
